title: Turn submit button in `st.chat_input` into stop button
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In ChatGPT and many other apps, the submit button in the chat input turns into a stop button after submitting. Clicking it interrupts the current LLM generation/streaming. We should have the same thing!

### Why?

Today, there's no way to interrupt an LLM generation in a Streamlit app. That can be annoying for long LLM messages. 

### How?

After submitting a message, the submit button should turn into a stop button. Clicking it should interrupt the current run, maybe simply by calling `st.stop` under the hood? If the run is interrupted or finished, the stop button should turn back into a submit button. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

## Update

Streamlit 1.59+ will have a `submit_mode` parameter for `st.chat_input` that controls widget behavior after submission while the script is running:

- "submit" (default): The widget remains fully enabled after submission. Users can submit new messages while the script is running (existing behavior).
- "disable": The widget is automatically disabled after submission and re-enabled when the run completes. This prevents users from interrupting ongoing operations like LLM streaming.
- "stop": The submit button transforms into a stop button while the script runs, allowing users to halt execution (like the app's "Stop" button). The text area is disabled during the run.
